notes: The catalogue entry for arduino-leonardo lists no ports; I used the pin labels printed on the board (2-6, 5V, GND.1), following the arduino-uno naming.

Bank mapping: the circuit image labels the top half of the breadboard rows j-f and the bottom half rows e-a. I therefore used bank 'b' (rows f-j) for the top half and bank 't' (rows a-e) for the bottom half. The rails are the top rail 'tp' (+, 5V) and the bottom rail 'bn' (GND).

Column positions were estimated from the image. Each button straddles the centre gap on columns 6/8, 11/13, 16/18, 21/23 and 26/28. Its right-hand column takes 5V from a red jumper from the top + rail. Its left-hand column in the lower half carries the signal wire and the pulldown resistor to the GND rail. Rail hole numbers are approximate.
Button to pin mapping, taken from the image and schematic: buttons 1-5 go to pins 6, 5, 4, 3 and 2. Per the sketch, pin 2 is up, 3 is down, 4 is left, 5 is right and 6 is the mouse click.
The pulldown resistors are 10k ohm. The pushbutton's pin 1 is taken as the upper (rows f-j) side and pin 2 as the lower side. The two right-hand legs are on the same side as the 5V jumper.
The micro-USB cable to the computer is included as a part with unspecified ports.
